title: Language pack
description: One language's (optionally one locale's) contribution to language quality: which external bodies are authoritative for what, which durable rules the pack asserts, and how domain terms are rendered. AES-V2.17 / SUE-607. The methodology this pack plugs into is language-agnostic and lives in docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md; nothing in that document may be restated here, and nothing here may be generalised to another language. A pack grants craft and correctness authority over language only. It never grants factual authority over a claim (Source is not Reference, V2-EDITORIAL-LEARNING-CORE.md §2).

pack_id.description: BCP-47-style id. Also the filename stem under editorial/profiles/language/.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language subtag. Separate from pack_id so a future en-US and en-GB share a language while differing as locales.

status.description: draft — written but not yet governing generation. active — governing, and therefore requiring a calibration version to change materially.

doc_ref.description: Repo-relative path to the pack's prose contract. The JSON is the machine surface; the prose explains the phenomena and must not contradict it.

calibration_ref.description: The calibration version that activated the pack's current empirical content, or null while status is draft. Normative rules do not need one — a standards body is not calibration evidence.

authorities.description: External bodies and works this pack rests on. Each records what it governs AND what it does not, so a public-language guide cannot quietly become a literary style authority.

rules.description: Durable language statements. Every rule carries exactly one authority class and routes to exactly one layer.

terminology.description: Domain terms: the canonical concept, its accepted rendering in this language, and any audience-facing surface form. An audience alias changes the wording, never the concept it maps to.

not_authoritative_for.description: Explicit non-scope. A pack that claims authority over facts, over another language, or over publication is misdeclared.

authority_class.description: What kind of thing would have to change for a statement to stop being true. Precedence is fixed in docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §2 and is not restated per rule.

source_class.description: What an external work can establish. NORMATIVE_STANDARD is codified correctness. STRONG_GUIDANCE is official but advisory. EMPIRICAL_REFERENCE is well-edited example material — evidence of craft, never of correctness. TERMINOLOGY_AUTHORITY is a canonical term list.

layer.description: The feedback-routing layer a failure against this rule routes to. Ids are owned by editorial/feedback-routing.json and are not redefined here.

generality.description: How far a rule's evidence actually reaches. shared requires cross-genre evidence; the *_local values keep a trait scoped to where it was observed. source_local is the default for anything seen in one publisher or institution and is never promoted as a side effect of being useful.

checkability.description: mechanical — a validator can decide it. review_guidance — a human or judge decides, and a confident automated verdict would be wrong. Declaring review guidance as mechanical is the failure this field exists to prevent.

does_not_govern.description: Mandatory and substantive. The commonest way this architecture fails is an authority silently widening past its remit.

scope.description: Where a rule applies. Genre and audience are independent axes and are listed independently; an empty or absent list means the rule is not scoped by that axis. A rule scoped to one audience is not thereby a genre rule.

statement.description: What the rule asserts, written so a Writer can act on it and a Reviewer can falsify it. Not a slogan.

authority_ref.description: The `authorities[].id` this rule derives from. Required in practice for every NORMATIVE rule: a normative rule with no standards body behind it is a corpus observation wearing a normative label.

evidence_refs.description: Reference-evaluation or corpus refs the rule was DERIVED from — `discovery` records only. Independent sources, per docs/architecture/LANGUAGE-QUALITY-ARCHITECTURE.md §6. A NORMATIVE rule does not need these and is not made stronger by them. See holdout_refs for the validation half.

holdout_refs.description: Reference-evaluation refs the rule was TESTED against — records whose corpus_role is `holdout`, never used to derive it. Separate from evidence_refs because the two are different acts: evidence_refs is where the trait came from, holdout_refs is what would have falsified it. Listing a holdout record under evidence_refs destroys the holdout and is rejected; listing a discovery record here is rejected for the same reason in reverse. A rule that reaches past the one source it was observed in needs at least one of each — corroboration by a second independent institution is what distinguishes a language trait from one publisher's habit.

holdout_result.description: How the rule fared against material never used to derive it. not_yet_tested is honest; passing it off as validated is not.

adopt_verdict.description: adopt — apply it. avoid — the opposite behaviour is the defect signature. do_not_copy — the trait is recognizable wording or a house signature and must not be reproduced even though it was observed in good writing.

canonical.description: The concept's authoritative name. This is what every alias must still map to.

rendering.description: The accepted form in this language, where one exists and differs from the canonical name.

rendering_policy.description: keep_source — the source-language form is what a competent practitioner uses. translate — the localised form is. either — both are current and the piece may choose. See editorial/voice.md §1: the test is which form a reader in the field reaches for without mentally translating.

audience_alias.description: A plainer surface form for one audience. The alias replaces the wording; `canonical` above still fixes the concept, and an alias that names a different concept is a domain_terminology defect, not an audience adaptation.
